key_insight: The classical 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm stabilizes in linear time, with a proven upper bound of 5(n-1) rounds, matching the known Ω(n) lower bound up to constants.
engineering_relevance: This gives a sharper worst-case guarantee for graph refinement routines used in graph isomorphism, graph learning, and combinatorial optimization pipelines.
method: Analyze stabilization rounds of the classical 2-WL color refinement process.
Derive a new linear upper bound of 5(n-1) iterations.
Extend the argument to k-dimensional WL, obtaining O(n^{k-1}/(k-2)! + n^{k-2}) for k ≥ 3.
evidence_signal: The paper’s evidence is theoretical: it improves the prior O(n log n) bound and matches the established Ω(n) lower bound asymptotically.
watch_item: The bound is worst-case and asymptotic; actual runtime depends on graph size, implementation details, and how the refinement is instantiated in practice.
paper_title: The Classical Weisfeiler-Leman Algorithm Stabilizes in $O(n)$ Rounds
